description: Found by the fz-iqp.4 builder's probes against Elixir 1.19.4 (not re-probed by me). fz reads names with XID_Start/XID_Continue (unicode-ident). Elixir builds its set from general categories plus Other_ID_Start/Continue, minus Pattern_Syntax and the UTS 39 restricted identifier types (lib/elixir/unicode/tokenizer.ex). Differences seen: the ligature U+FB01 as a variable and a followed by U+00AA are rejected by Elixir and accepted by fz; Bopomofo U+3105 is rejected by Elixir and accepted by fz. Two related gaps: Elixir folds the micro sign U+00B5 to Greek mu U+03BC in names (fz keeps two variables); Elixir re-validates the NFC form of a name (invalid_normalized) and fz does not. Signal: a differential run against String.Tokenizer over the identifier code points, as the mixed-script rule had (about 520,000 names, 0 mismatches).
title: A name's characters are Elixir's identifier set, not XID
